author: BBC News
description:
Yemens' civil war has flared up in recent weeks, as the Iran-backed Houthi movement seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast, in a rapid offensive.
 
Oil prices have risen on fears of further disruption to the global economy, following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.
 
Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed on both sides during the Houthis' advance, which came after the collapse of a four-year informal ceasefire. The UN says more than 120,000 people have been displaced by the escalation.
 
But who are the Houthis, what are they targeting, and what will the impact be on the rest of the world? 
The Security Brief's Christian Fraser and Mikey Kay explain.

author: BBC News
description:
Has Donald Trump just rebranded AI? This week, the US President declared that "Artificial Intelligence" sounds too fake and should be renamed "Super Intelligence" instead. 
 
Whether "SI" catches on remains to be seen, but as the world debates what to call the technology, a much bigger question is emerging: who gets to control it?
 
In this episode of AI Decoded we examine a pivotal week for artificial intelligence as Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping, with AI high on the agenda. 
 
Joining the panel are Parmy Olson, Bloomberg technology columnist and author of Supremacy, and Winston Ma, former executive at China Investment Corporation, alongside AI Decoded co-host Priya Lakhani. Together they explore the intensifying AI rivalry between the world's two superpowers, competing visions for regulating the technology, and whether international cooperation is still possible.

description:
After years spent sheltering from the public gaze, Hunter Biden re-entered the mainstream consciousness last summer via a surprise YouTube appearance alongside prominent alternative media figure Andrew Callaghan. The interview went viral, and ever since the embattled son of former president Joe Biden has seen his online reputation soar. 

On this episode, Matt and Marianna track Biden Jr's journey from ridicule to redemption, and ask whether he has fumbled that newly found following with a dubious crypto enterprise, an all-too-familiar fall from grace in the age of the internet.  

Also this week, actor Channing Tatum has denied he is behind an Instagram 'burner' account which was critical of his ex-partners, despite being its only follower. 

Sleuths had discovered comments across several posts which appeared to support him while calling out Jenna Dewan, Zoe Kravitz and others.

We discuss the broader phenomenon of anonymous celeb-run accounts, examples of identities being uncovered,
title: What Channing Tatum tells us about the psychology of burner accounts | Top Comment Podcast

author: BBC News
description:
The US president has lost his court battle with CNN, Politico and MS NOW in the latest battle between Donald Trump and the media. What did the judge say and what happens next?

At the end of the last week Donald Trump banned three news outlets - CNN, Politico and MS Now - from reporting inside the White House. But the ban has been overturned - for now - in an emergency hearing by a federal judge, who ordered the banned journalists’ press credentials be immediately reinstated for 14 days.

It’s still not entirely clear what prompted Donald Trump to punish the outlets although it’s been reported that it may have been prompted by negative coverage he was shown by his aide, Natalie Harp.

In this episode, Justin, Anthony and Marianna speak to former CNN correspondent, anchor and bureau chief Frank Sesno, who is now a Journalism professor at The George Washington School of Media and Public Affairs. The latest row comes at a difficult moment for the president who’s fighting historically low
title: What next after US President Donald Trump loses his fight with the press? | BBC Americast

Health workers have called it "a huge leap forward for patients" that will "completely transform" how brain tumours are diagnosed

Services provided by state-owned telecoms operator Ethio Telecom have been completely cut, although those from the much smaller private firm Safaricom remain operational. 
 
Internet monitoring group NetBlocks earlier posted on X that network data indicated a sub-national internet shutdown in northern Tigray.
 
Clashes between Tigrayan forces and their allies and Ethiopia's federal troops broke out on Wednesday, prompting heightened tension and reports of panic buying.
 
During the two-year civil which ended in 2022, Tigray was totally cut off from the outside world.
 
Limited access to cash, food and medicine pushed hundreds of thousands into famine-like conditions.
 
The BBC has contacted Ethiopian authorities for comment.

The pontiff cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the Élysée Palace, following an hour of talks with President Emmanuel Macron.
 
Large crowds expected throughout the trip, reflecting an enthusiasm that the Church attributes to growing spirituality among the French and other Europeans.
 
The highpoint of his visit is set to be a giant Mass attended by more than half a million people in Paris on Saturday.

description:
Pope Leo XIV embarks on a four-day visit to France on Friday, with the highpoint being a giant Mass attended by more than half a million people in central Paris.
 
For Saturday's afternoon celebration, an altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde and a large area around the Champs-Élysées sealed off by police.
 
President Emmanuel Macron greeted the Pope at Orly airport on Friday morning, and is due to hold talks with him at the Élysée Palace on geopolitical issues and artificial intelligence (AI) later. He will also deliver a speech with the Pope in Metz.
 
However, the president will not be at any of the Pope's Masses, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.
